release.title: 2018 SIPP Data
release.reference_period_excerpt: 2018 SIPP data files covering the reference period January - December 2017.
release.panel_excerpt: 2018 SIPP includes Wave 1 of the 2018 Panel only.
release.update_excerpt: 2018 SIPP data were updated on 7/24/2025 to correct an issue with Social Security Income Processing.
release.local_release_caveat: The local file is user-supplied. Its content hash is recorded at preparation time, not compared with an official Census hash. The currently advertised release date is not an authenticated local file version.

schema.local_header_observation: All 4942 header names and their order match the official schema. First 240 rows contain SPANEL=2018 and SWAVE=1; runtime checks validate the entire input.
schema.calendar_year_field: No reference-calendar-year field in the schema; reference year is established by the release documentation, conditional on verified SPANEL=2018 and SWAVE=1.

selected_fields.name: RMNUMJOBS
selected_fields.definition: Recode of number of jobs held within the reference month.

selected_fields.name: RIN_UNIV
selected_fields.definition: Monthly indicator that respondent is in survey frame universe

selected_fields.name: TMWKHRS
selected_fields.definition: Average number of hours worked per week at all jobs held during the reference month.
selected_fields.universe: At least one job on job-lines 1-7 was held during the reference month.

selected_fields.name: TPEARN
selected_fields.definition: Sum of earnings and profits/losses from all jobs, varying with the number of days in the month (comparable to RPEARN in 1996, 2001, and 2014 SIPP panels).
selected_fields.universe: At least one job on job-lines 1-8 was held during the reference month.

dictionaries.missing_excerpt: Not in universe will be "." for numeric variables and blank for character variables.
dictionaries.local_missing_observation: First 240 rows include adult no-job months with RMNUMJOBS=0 and blank TPEARN/TMWKHRS, so the parser accepts both blank and dot numeric missing tokens.
dictionaries.topcoding_excerpt: When topcoding assets, earnings, and medical expenditures, values at the top of the distribution are replaced by the mean (or median) of those values.

earnings_note.excerpt: The only difference is that TPEARN is processed to vary with the number of days in the month, while TPEARN_ALT is processed not to vary with the number of days in the month.
